item.description:
Two toolbar refinements for macOS 27 and sharper quit diagnostics.

  • The month selector breathes. On macOS 27 the month label sat tight against the edge of its toolbar bubble. It now has the same inset and weight as Apple’s own toolbar menus (Pages’ Zoom menu was the reference), and drops down with a single chevron like they do.
  • No more “Pits quit unexpectedly” pop-up. It guessed at a cause it couldn’t know, and it could appear when nothing had gone wrong. Pits still notes an unclean exit in the system log; it just doesn’t interrupt you about it.
  • Quit logging names the caller. When something other than you asks Pits to quit, the log now records which part of the system did the asking. This is aimed at the “Pits vanished after waking the Mac” problem, which was seen again on October 12 one second after a lid-open wake reshuffled the displays.
